import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import norm, t, skewnorm
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Edit this list to change the priors.
strategies = [
    {'title': 'Aggressive fourth downs', 'family': 'normal', 'most_plausible': 0.25, 'params': {'mu': 0.25, 'sigma': 0.1531}},
    {'title': 'First-down play-action', 'family': 'normal', 'most_plausible': 0.22, 'params': {'mu': 0.22, 'sigma': 0.1633}},
    {'title': 'Two-high shells', 'family': 'normal', 'most_plausible': 0.18, 'params': {'mu': 0.18, 'sigma': 0.1429}},
    {'title': 'Timeout to kill chaos', 'family': 'student_t', 'most_plausible': 0.0, 'params': {'nu': 4, 'mu': 0.0, 'sigma': 0.155}},
    {'title': 'No-huddle bursts after explosives', 'family': 'student_t', 'most_plausible': 0.08, 'params': {'nu': 4, 'mu': 0.08, 'sigma': 0.137}},
    {'title': 'Disguise-and-pressure mix', 'family': 'student_t', 'most_plausible': 0.11, 'params': {'nu': 4, 'mu': 0.11, 'sigma': 0.1261}},
]

def make_dist(item):
    fam = item['family']
    p = item['params']
    if fam == 'normal':
        return norm(loc=p['mu'], scale=p['sigma'])
    if fam == 'student_t':
        return t(df=p['nu'], loc=p['mu'], scale=p['sigma'])
    if fam == 'skew_normal':
        return skewnorm(a=p['alpha'], loc=p['xi'], scale=p['omega'])
    raise ValueError(f'Unknown family: {fam}')

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(16, 9))
axes = axes.ravel()

for ax, item in zip(axes, strategies):
    dist = make_dist(item)
    lo = dist.ppf(0.001)
    hi = dist.ppf(0.999)
    xs = np.linspace(lo, hi, 800)
    ys = dist.pdf(xs)
    q025 = dist.ppf(0.025)
    q975 = dist.ppf(0.975)

    ax.plot(xs, ys, color='navy', lw=2)
    ax.axvspan(q025, q975, color='skyblue', alpha=0.25, label='95% interval')
    mp = item['most_plausible']
    ax.axvline(mp, color='red', ls='--', lw=1.5, label='most plausible')
    ax.plot([mp], [dist.pdf(mp)], 'ro')
    ax.set_title(item['title'])
    ax.set_xlabel('Change in own scoring margin (points)')
    ax.set_ylabel('Density')
    ax.grid(alpha=0.2)
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)

    print(item['title'], item['family'], item['params'])

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
